articleTitle: The benefits of dry air preservation power plants
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Maintenance Practices for Power Generation
abstract: The preservation of power station units in the cold shut-down condition for prolonged periods is a significant problem because of condensation and corrosion. A simple way to obtain air of low relative humidity, is by means of a sorption dehumidifier. The system is dried using the vacuum method and dry air is applied at certain points of the system to be preserved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: C&I systems for predictive maintenance in ScottishPower's power stations
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Maintenance Practices for Power Generation
abstract: The capital cost of modern power stations is such that it is essential that they operate at maximum output for as much as the time as possible, to optimise revenue. At present, routine maintenance is carried out on all of the strategic items of a plant in order to ensure that these are available at all times. The author looks at the ways that ScottishPower intends to prevent in-service failures using on-line diagnosis and on-line fault finding.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Maintenance in an industrial CHP station
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Maintenance Practices for Power Generation
abstract: Merseyside power station (MPS) was built in 1957 to supply steam and power to Unilever and third party companies in the Port Sunlight and Bromborough areas. There are four maintenance areas: the engine generator; the water treatment plant; the boiler control and instrumentation systems; and the HV system. Preventive maintenance is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A review of electrical plant maintenance practices in power stations
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Maintenance Practices for Power Generation
abstract: Maintenance of power stations is essential, but there is a cost penalty. Accumulated experience and diagnostic testing enables outage work to be planned ahead. Major plant spares shorten outages and improve availability. The main generator and the generator transformer of a power station are looked at in particular.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Turbo generator plant: the developing role of the original equipment manufacturer
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Maintenance Practices for Power Generation
abstract: To power station operators the achievement of reliability and availability of the power generating plant is of primary concern. To this end the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) must assume greater responsibility for the operation of his plant in the field. The OEM should agree and implement with the operator a long term strategic plan for inspection and maintenance of generators, coupled with the introduction, wherever possible, of improved modern day designs and materials to older machines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Maintenance practices for gas turbines in power generation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Maintenance Practices for Power Generation
abstract: The author looks at the significant maintenance practices of the GE-type heavy duty gas turbines in terms of megawatts, give outputs in the range of 12/220 MW. For the gas turbine in regular operation, there are basically two types of maintenance, namely, running and shutdown. The author concentrates on shutdown maintenance including hot gas path inspection and combustion inspection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Maintenance Practices for Power Generation
abstract: A turbogenerator is a rotating, high speed, complex precision machine which generates electrical power. The use of preventive maintenance can reduce the number and duration of unplanned outages by a process of periodic inspections, tests, and component refurbishment, replacement or upgrading. The author looks at how the Turbine Generator Service Organisation operates to provide optimum overhauls of turbogenerators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Alternator rotor cracking problems and their solutions
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Maintenance Practices for Power Generation
abstract: Heysham nuclear power station has two 660 MW turbogenerators manufactured by NEI Parsons. The rotor is an alloy steel forging with field winding slots cut along the full length of the round rotor body. In January 1988 a rotor of similar type to Heysham's operating at Drax was taken out of service and found to have a major crack. During September a second rotor at Drax was also found to have a major crack. The author looks at maintenance and inspection techniques used at Heysham to make sure that the same cracking does not occur.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Framatome services to nuclear power plants
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Maintenance Practices for Power Generation
abstract: Framatome is one of the world's leading designers, manufacturers and exporters of PWR nuclear steam supply systems (NSSS). To adapt to slow-downs in nuclear power programmes, Framatome has succeeded in converting itself into a multinational group with diversified high technology activities. It now provides design and engineering services to nuclear electric utilities to introduce improvements through the constant development of nuclear power technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
